newsitem.title: netherlands: FOCUS-Business info drives 16 pct VNU earnings rise.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Business info drives 16 pct VNU earnings rise.

text.p: Buoyant earnings from business information outweighed a small loss on commercial television and flat newspaper profits, lifting publisher VNU to a 15.6 percent rise in ordinary net income for 1996.

VNU -- whose businesses span glossy consumer magazines to electronic on-line delivery of marketing data -- said on Tuesday that net profit from ordinary operations rose to 316 million guilders ($166.1 million) from 274 million in 1995.
The dividend was raised to 0.55 guilders per share from 0.48 guilders in 1995 and VNU said it expected a further increase in profits and earnings per share in 1997.

Overall net profit, including extraordinary items, fell to 322 million guilders from 430 million in 1995 when it was swollen by an extraordinary gain of 157 million guilders on the sale of U.S. financial information unit Disclosure.
VNU's results were broadly in line with expectations but analysts were cheered by the growing contribution from business information where operating profits rose by over 40 percent.
Consumer magazines saw operating profit rise 17 percent, while regional newspapers gained just one percent and commercial television made a small loss due to fierce competition.
Magazines were buoyed by higher subscription and advertising revenues in the Netherlands and a reorganisation in Belgium.
Newspaper profits were below VNU's own expectations because of higher paper costs, the launch of regional television projects and one-off merger costs.

VNU chairman Joep Brentjens told a news conference that international expansion of marketing information services (MIS) -- one of the fastest growing areas within business information -- was one of the group's strategic priorities.
"We will certainly invest a lot in (MIS) in the coming years and we expect to see a lot of growth in this area," he said.
Business information as a whole generated 43 percent of VNU's operating profits in 1996, up from seven percent in 1992.
"This is the growth area for VNU. That is what we saw last year and we expect it to remain so," finance manager Frans Cremers said.

Brentjens said demand for VNU's marketing information services for advertisers, advertising agencies and media groups was growing strongly in the United States and that VNU now planned to expand into other regions from this strong U.S. base.
"We plan to start operating worldwide in marketing information services," he said.
Analysts said that while VNU's results met expectations they were pleased with the increasing quality of earnings and in particular the strong performance by business information.
"I regard that as very positive because the mix of sales is increasingly shifting to business-to-business," said Andre Moons of ING Barings.
On an overall lower Amsterdam bourse, VNU shares were among a handful of advancers, showing a slim gain of 0.10 guilders at 41.00 in late afternoon trade.
